records.title: General intelligence
records.milestone: A general-purpose AI will independently demonstrate skilled-human performance across a broad set of unfamiliar cognitive tasks.
resolution: Two evaluation teams independent of the model provider test the same frozen general-purpose system on independently created tasks. Each preregisters task-construction rules, scoring and human recruitment before testing, then publishes its protocol, human comparison, tools, time budgets and results.

Each evaluation covers language, mathematics, coding, factual synthesis, scientific reasoning, visual-spatial reasoning, planning, social reasoning, learning new rules and switching between tasks. Each domain contains at least 100 tasks created after the system was frozen. No task-specific retraining is allowed.

The system reaches or exceeds the median of relevant skilled adult participants in every domain under the same stated time allowance. This is our operational AGI threshold, not a claim that every definition of AGI has been satisfied.
records.rationale: We expect broader reasoning, memory and tool use to improve over several more development cycles. We put our date at the end of 2031 because unfamiliar tasks, consistency across domains and independent replication are a much higher bar than a strong benchmark score. This is our judgement about the remaining work, not a trend line fitted to the sources.
records.uncertainty: Very uncertain timing. A generalisation breakthrough could bring this forward sharply, while persistent failures on unfamiliar tasks could put it beyond 2031. Our test is a declared working definition, not an industry standard.
records.earlier: Independent teams reproduce skilled-human performance across newly created domains without task-specific tuning or undisclosed human help.
records.later: Public benchmark gains fail to transfer to fresh tasks, or broad competence continues to depend on specialist retraining and extensive human correction.

evidence.limit: Adaptive reasoning is only part of general intelligence. This benchmark alone cannot resolve our broader forecast.

records.title: Agents at work
records.milestone: AI agents will run repeatable business workflows across at least ten organisations, with people managing exceptions.
resolution: Customer-confirmed or independently evaluated public reports name ten organisations across at least three sectors. Each runs two distinct production workflows spanning at least two business systems.

Each workflow reports at least 1,000 consecutive eligible cases over at least 90 days. At least 80% finish without a person executing workflow steps. Eligibility, acceptance tests and escalation rules are fixed before the reporting period.

People may authorise consequential decisions and handle exceptions. Reports include failures and escalations in the denominator. This predicts repeatable operation at ten organisations, not majority adoption or unattended businesses.
records.rationale: Bounded workflow execution already exists. We expect the next two years to turn isolated deployments into repeatable operations across sectors, with permissions, recovery and ownership becoming part of the product. End-2028 is our forecast for that operational milestone.
records.uncertainty: Timing remains uncertain. Vendor case studies rarely publish consecutive-case failure and intervention data, so the milestone could occur before enough public evidence exists to verify it.
records.earlier: Customer-confirmed 90-day results show high autonomous completion across multiple systems and sectors, including failures and recovery costs.
records.later: Manual rescue, fragile integrations or operating costs prevent teams expanding beyond isolated queues.

evidence.title: Salesforce and Air India: workflow expansion

records.title: Robotics
records.milestone: Adaptable robots will perform several useful jobs routinely across factories and warehouses, with demonstrated operating economics.
resolution: One commercially available robot platform using a shared general-purpose control model runs for six months at ten production sites belonging to at least three unrelated customers. records.uncertainty: The date is uncertain because reliability, safety and manufacturing must improve together. Strong demonstrations or a product launch would not be enough to count this as achieved.
records.earlier: Customers publish six-month multi-task fleet results, lower intervention rates and repeat purchases supported by full operating costs.
records.later: Maintenance, low utilisation, teleoperation or poor transfer between tasks keeps the cost of successful work above the existing process.

records.title: Software creation

records.title: Education

records.uncertainty: Benefits may depend heavily on tutor design, subject and student group. Immediate performance with assistance can improve without producing durable independent learning.
records.earlier: Multi-site trials show replicated gains on delayed, unassisted tests across learner groups.
records.later: Gains disappear without AI, fail to transfer, or depend on levels of human support that do not scale.

evidence.title: Kestin and colleagues: AI tutoring trial

evidence.limit: The short intervention at one institution does not demonstrate long-term retention or broad institutional scale.

evidence.finding: GXO and Agility say Digit will expand from one Georgia operation to two additional US sites in early 2027. The existing site has moved more than 100,000 totes. New deployments will begin with Digit 4 and later migrate to Digit 5.
evidence.limit: The additional sites are prospective. One repeated material-handling task at one current site is not a six-month, ten-site, multi-task shared-model record. Intervention rates and full cost per successful task remain undisclosed.

evidence.title: Agility: deployment support expansion and customer claims
evidence.finding: Agility reports current work with GXO, Schaeffler and Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, four additional customers, a new pilot and more than $300 million in multi-year Digit 5 orders subject to contractual milestones.
evidence.limit: These are vendor-reported customer and order claims. Pilots, conditional orders and support capacity do not establish customer-confirmed intervention-free cycles, adaptable tasks, six-month continuity or operating economics.

records.later: Maintenance, low utilisation, teleoperation or poor transfer between tasks keeps the cost of successful work above the existing process.
records.milestone: Adaptable robots will perform several useful jobs routinely across factories and warehouses, with demonstrated operating economics.
records.rationale: We retain end-2031. Expansion to named sites and customers is stronger commercial evidence than a laboratory demonstration. Most of the new operating record is still planned for 2027, uses a generation transition and covers narrow material handling. The reports do not satisfy our shared-model task breadth, six-month reliability, intervention disclosure or full-cost threshold, so the target stays unchanged.
resolution: One commercially available robot platform using a shared general-purpose control model runs for six months at ten production sites belonging to at least three unrelated customers. It performs at least three materially different task families overall and at least two at each site. Customers demonstrate a new task learned from instructions or examples without writing task-specific control code.
Customer-confirmed reporting shows at least 95% of task cycles completed without human intervention. The reporting period, task mix, failures and supervised or teleoperated time are disclosed.

Customer-published cost per successful task matches or beats the incumbent process, including maintenance and supervision. This is a commercial-site milestone, not a prediction of routine household humanoids.
records.title: Robotics
records.uncertainty: The date is uncertain because reliability, safety and manufacturing must improve together. Strong demonstrations or a product launch would not be enough to count this as achieved.

records.earlier: Organisations publish consecutive-ticket results with little manual rescue and reliable post-deployment checks.

evidence.title: OpenAI: Patch the Planet vulnerability response
evidence.finding: OpenAI reports that an AI-assisted researcher identified a critical PHP flaw before public disclosure. The programme combined model access with security experts, maintainers, tests, fixes, infrastructure protections and coordinated guidance.
evidence.limit: This is a selected security case with expert review and coordinated human delivery. It reports neither all attempted findings nor consecutive routine tickets, manual code corrections, approved deployments, rollbacks or seven-day monitoring across ten organisations.

evidence.title: OpenAI: Amp's software and post-shipping ambitions
evidence.finding: Amp reports agent use for planning, coding, documentation and design. Its stated next step is to encompass more work before and after coding.
evidence.limit: A wider product workflow and customer testimony do not show consecutive tickets reaching approved deployment and seven-day monitoring without manual code correction. The account contains no qualifying 90-day ticket cohort.

records.later: Review effort, rollback rates or legacy-system failures prevent agents reliably completing the whole delivery cycle.
records.milestone: Coding agents will take most routine software tickets from specification to monitored production in at least ten organisations, with human approval.
records.rationale: We retain end-2027 as an assertive forecast. The vulnerability response shows that agents can contribute to valuable software and security work inside a human-led process. It does not measure routine specification-to-production delivery or expose a failure denominator. Broader lifecycle ambition remains prospective, leaving no defensible basis for moving the date.
resolution: Ten named organisations each publish customer-confirmed or independently evaluated results for at least 100 consecutive eligible tickets over at least 90 days. Eligibility is fixed before assignment: routine fixes or small features estimated at no more than one engineer-day.

More than half reach implementation, tests, review responses, approved deployment and seven days of monitoring without people writing or correcting the code. Humans still set requirements, review and authorise release.

Failed deployments, rollbacks and manually rescued tickets remain in the denominator. Merged pull requests alone do not meet the milestone. This does not predict autonomous ownership of all engineering work.
records.title: Software creation
records.uncertainty: This is an assertive forecast. Repository preparation, review effort and access to credible post-deployment results could delay verification. The date is our judgement, not a provider's commitment.

records.earlier: Multi-site trials show replicated gains on delayed, unassisted tests across learner groups.

evidence.title: Oreopoulos and Low: two-year Khanmigo school trial
evidence.finding: Across 18 Tennessee middle schools, assignment to Khan Academy with Khanmigo raised achievement by about 0.06 to 0.08 standard deviations over a school year. Tutor engagement was sparse. The paper discusses preregistration and school exclusions.
evidence.limit: This is a bundled practice intervention, not an isolated randomised AI increment. Similar gains occur with non-AI practice. These are not two independent replications, and no qualifying eight-week post-intervention outcome is established here.

evidence.title: Oreopoulos and colleagues: NUMI mastery experiment
evidence.finding: The randomised experiment covers over 6,000 middle-school students. AI improved correction after mistakes while slowing progress. Delayed learning gains were limited, with the clearest signal on practised material in a mastery workflow.
evidence.limit: The delayed assessment is one week later, not eight weeks. This short intervention and the same district and overlapping research team do not provide independent term-long replications. Better assisted corrections are not durable learning by themselves.

evidence.title: Liu and colleagues: university tutoring counterevidence
evidence.finding: The randomised university study of 2,379 undergraduates reports lower grades and participation with access to a course-integrated AI tutor.
evidence.limit: One university and a working paper do not establish universal harm. Its access effect complements the school evidence without meeting the delayed unassisted-learning test.

records.later: Gains disappear without AI, fail to transfer, or depend on levels of human support that do not scale.
records.milestone: Generative AI tutoring will show repeatable learning gains that last after the AI is put away, across schools or colleges.
records.rationale: We retain end-2029 with substantial uncertainty. A fresh primary-source search found no later outcome study that changes the mixed evidence. The positive school interventions still do not isolate replicated, term-long AI effects with eight-week unassisted follow-up, while the university trial remains counterevidence from one setting. The declared durable-learning threshold is unmet and the target stays unchanged.
resolution: Two independently evaluated, preregistered randomised trials of generative AI tutoring collectively cover at least 2,000 learners across at least 20 schools or colleges, with an intervention lasting at least one academic term. Each compares against a non-AI control with comparable teaching and learning time.

Both trials show statistically positive effects on unassisted assessments at least eight weeks after the intervention. Their combined standardised effect is at least 0.2, using an inverse-variance weighted mean of the reported primary outcomes.

Human teachers and safeguarding remain in place. The reports disclose attrition and assistance. This predicts demonstrated durable learning gains, not the replacement of teachers, schools or credentials.
records.title: Education
records.uncertainty: Benefits may depend heavily on tutor design, subject and student group. Immediate performance with assistance can improve without producing durable independent learning.
